**Visual Analysis:**

- **Affected part**: Sugarcane leaf, close-up view
- **Key features**:
  - Prominent **bright yellow/golden midrib** - the central vein area is distinctly yellowed
  - The lamina on one side (left) is bleached pale/cream-white
  - The lamina on the right edge shows orange-yellow discoloration
  - The central green zone persists along the midrib axis
  - No discrete spots, pustules, or pencil-line lesions are visible
  - No obvious curling, twisting, or top rot

**Reasoning:**

The dominant diagnostic feature is the **striking yellow midrib** with surrounding laminar discoloration spreading outward. This is precisely the hallmark sign of **Yellow_Leaf** disease (YLD caused by sugarcane yellow leaf virus): *"Midrib yellowing (mild to severe) is a hallmark sign... young leaves show bright midrib yellowing while matured leaves show extensive discoloration of lamina."*

- **Leaf_Scald** is ruled out — no pencil-line streak, no inward curling
- **Yellow_Spot / Brown_Spot** are ruled out — no discrete lesion spots
- **Pokkah_Boeng** ruled out — no twisted/malformed leaves or top rot
- **Streak_Mosaic / Sugarcane_Mosaic_Virus** would show streaking/mosaic patterns, not midrib-centered yellowing
- **Grassy_Shoot** would show bushy tillering, not this leaf pattern

The pattern — green midrib vein flanked by bright yellow, with pale lamina extending to the margin — is classic YLD.
